reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, full DeviceDefinition StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, relevant shared behavior context, and selected R4/R6 package StructureDefinition elements for the high-leverage paths. Direct behavior findings were absent. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only because the assigned artifact is DeviceDefinition, not Resource or DomainResource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 DeviceDefinition was trial-use/FMM 0, so there is weak standards-stability pressure to preserve every R4 field or representation. That substantially lowers the burden to justify a broad R6 redesign, but it does not eliminate compatibility concern for device catalog, UDI/regulatory, manufacturer, support, endpoint, and version data where silent semantic changes or expert-dependent migration can affect safety and business workflows.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 keeps DeviceDefinition's identity but remodels it into a canonical device catalog artifact; a migration program is unavoidable, while several low-cost or safety-relevant compatibility preservations still deserve attention.

reasoning.thesisMd: DeviceDefinition is not removed, but it is not a mostly stable resource with a few isolated breaks. R6 adds mandatory lifecycle/status metadata, repurposes `url` and `version` toward canonical-artifact semantics, moves or replaces classification/type/version/property/language structures, and removes or reworks manufacturer, owner/support contact, capability/conformance, parent-device, packaging, and physical-characteristic surfaces. A real R4 implementation cannot rely on validation drift or simple generated-model regeneration; it needs a resource-level migration policy.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a same-identity major model remodel. Some transforms are mechanical, such as mapping a populated R4 `type` into one R6 `classification.type` or splitting multi-valued properties into repeated R6 property rows. Other transforms require policy or domain judgment: assigning required `status`, deciding whether a manufacturer string should become an Organization reference, remapping removed name-type codes, separating device/software versions from business definition version, distinguishing device endpoint URL from canonical URL, and representing support contacts, ownership, communication capabilities, packaging quantity, parent relationships, and physical characteristics in the new model.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the resource already needs a migration program, preserving any one old path will not make most populated R4 instances automatically R6-valid. That lowers the leverage of preserving local fields that would create duplicate representations, such as keeping both top-level `type` and repeatable `classification`, or both old property value lists and new `value[x]`. It does not justify ignoring avoidable breaks. The highest-value compatibility work is to preserve or explicitly map data where the R6 redesign creates silent semantic traps, lossy mappings, or unnecessary identity-management decisions.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most standards-review-worthy alternatives are targeted rather than wholesale rollback: avoid same-name semantic repurposing for `url` and `version`; retain a display/string manufacturer option or transitional alias while encouraging Organization references; carry forward removed `deviceName.type` codes as deprecated concepts or provide an official ConceptMap; preserve explicit support/owner/online-information roles or define standard extensions; and provide formal maps for capability/conformance and parent/packaging/physical-characteristic conversion. By contrast, retaining every removed field indefinitely would conflict with the R6 canonical/catalog model and is harder to justify for FMM 0 content.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: There are no direct OperationDefinitions, SearchParameters, or HttpRestBehavior findings assigned to DeviceDefinition. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant background for implementers using generic `$validate`, `$meta`, `$convert`, `_profile`, and related infrastructure, but they should not drive this resource-level conclusion or inflate DeviceDefinition-specific break severity.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is already unavoidable and that the shape is `major-model-remodel` with high confidence. I do not fully agree with the selected leverage label `migration-program-dominates`: for this same-identity resource, the broad migration program reduces the value of preserving duplicate local fields, but several Revisit findings still identify low-cost or safety/business-significant preservation points. The better resource posture is `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural shape because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions directly show the path, type, cardinality, and binding changes. Confidence is lower for prevalence and exact intended semantics because the local inputs do not include official DeviceDefinition change notes, production instance statistics, terminology-server expansions, or authoritative cross-version ConceptMaps, and the R6 input is a ballot package.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds mandatory DeviceDefinition.status
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 had no `status`; R6 requires a publication-status code. This alone means every R4 instance needs at least a status assignment before strict R6 validation. The `unknown` code makes the break more tolerable and the canonical-artifact lifecycle goal is coherent, so this is not the strongest avoidable-break candidate, but it is a clear driver of the unavoidable migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: manufacturer[x] was renamed and narrowed to a Reference-only manufacturer
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 allowed `manufacturerString`; R6 requires `Reference(Organization)`. Manufacturer identity is central to device catalogs and regulatory/UDI contexts, and converting a string into an Organization can require local master-data decisions. A low-cost preservation path, such as retaining a manufacturer display string or transitional choice, would reduce migration friction without preventing richer references.

findingConsiderations.title: deviceName.type changed from required primitive code to extensible CodeableConcept with a reduced local code system
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is both a wire-format change and a terminology shrink. R4 required primitive codes including values such as manufacturer/model/UDI-label name categories, while R6 uses CodeableConcept with fewer local concepts. The structural migration is easy, but dropped codes create avoidable semantic mapping work; deprecated concepts or an official ConceptMap would be valuable.

findingConsiderations.title: DeviceDefinition.type was removed and replaced by repeatable classification.type
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The top-level type-to-classification remodel is a major sign that the R6 resource is a richer catalog/classification model. For a single R4 type the migration can often be mechanical, and keeping both old and new fields would create duplicate representations, so this mostly supports the resource-level migration conclusion rather than a strong preservation demand.

findingConsiderations.title: DeviceDefinition.version changed from repeatable device versions to a single canonical business version
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `version` is one of the most important avoidable breaks. R4 used repeatable `version` for available device/software versions; R6 uses singleton `version` for the business version of the DeviceDefinition, while device/software versions move elsewhere. Multiple R4 values become invalid, and a single old value can silently mean the wrong thing. This deserves standards review even though the broader resource migration is unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: property values changed from repeatable valueQuantity/valueCode lists to a mandatory single value[x] choice
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 property values were separate repeatable quantity and code lists, while R6 requires exactly one broader `value[x]`. This breaks instances and generated APIs, but it also establishes a cleaner one-property/one-value representation with more datatypes. Once the R6 property model is accepted, splitting multi-valued R4 properties is a local migration chore rather than a high-leverage base-compatibility preservation point.

findingConsiderations.title: languageCode was replaced by outputLanguage with a primitive required all-languages binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a hard path/type/binding change for populated instances, but it is peripheral to the main device-catalog model and should usually be mechanically mappable for standard language tags. It supports the need for migration tooling but is not a major resource-level driver or preservation priority.

findingConsiderations.title: specialization and capability were removed and partially replaced by conformsTo and other R6 structures
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 specialization and capability carried communication standards, capabilities, and descriptive text. R6 `conformsTo` is more formal and useful, but not a one-for-one replacement for all capability descriptions. This is standards-review-worthy as a mapping and preservation problem: standard extensions, examples, or ConceptMaps could avoid lossy expert-dependent conversions without necessarily restoring the old R4 surface.

findingConsiderations.title: owner, contact, and onlineInformation support fields were removed or repurposed as publisher metadata
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 separated responsible owner/maintenance organization, support contacts, and online information. R6 publisher/contact metadata has different accountability semantics. Mis-migrating operational support contacts into publisher contact fields can create business and safety confusion, so this remains important despite FMM 0 and despite the broader remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: DeviceDefinition.url was repurposed from a device network address to a canonical artifact URL
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This potential hard break is especially concerning because old endpoint URIs may still satisfy the R6 `uri` type while being interpreted as canonical artifact identifiers. Silent semantic corruption of references, caching, publication, or lookup behavior is worse than a straightforward validation failure. A distinct canonical URL or endpoint field, or at least explicit transition guidance, is a high-value low-cost compatibility target.

findingConsiderations.title: parentDevice, quantity, and physicalCharacteristics were removed while R6 adds different relationship and packaging structures
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R6's `hasPart`, recursive packaging, and general property model are not simple aliases for R4 parentDevice, package quantity, and ProdCharacteristic data. Parent relationship direction and packaging quantity type can require domain judgment. This is a meaningful mapping risk, but preserving all old direct fields would create duplicate hierarchy and packaging models, so it is mainly a standards mapping/extension issue.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds many optional DeviceDefinition-specific backbones with no R4 base representation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The R6-only regulatory, linkage, usage, corrective-action, and billing structures matter for R6-to-R4 downgrade and extension strategy, but they are optional additions. They do not make old R4 DeviceDefinition instances invalid and should not drive the R4-to-R6 compatibility posture.

findingConsiderations.title: Many local elements became summary elements in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Summary flag changes can affect `_summary` response shape and generated metadata, but they do not invalidate R4 instances or remove content. They are context for implementation testing rather than a resource-level standards break.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource operation finding may affect generic validation workflows for any migrated DeviceDefinition instance, but it is not a DeviceDefinition-specific behavior finding and the assigned resource is neither Resource nor DomainResource. It did not change the resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search-parameter finding is relevant background for generic clients, but it is a base Resource/DomainResource issue rather than a local DeviceDefinition migration driver.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Create or publish an official R4-to-R6 DeviceDefinition migration package with StructureMaps/ConceptMaps covering status assignment, manufacturer string/reference policy, deviceName.type code migration, classification/type, deviceVersion/version, property values, conformsTo/capability, support contacts, and parent/packaging/physical-characteristic mappings.

Revisit same-name semantic reuse for `url` and `version`. At minimum, add explicit migration guidance and validation warnings that prevent R4 device endpoint URLs or device/software versions from being silently interpreted as canonical artifact identifiers or business versions.

Consider targeted transitional compatibility in the base model or standard extensions for high-friction data: manufacturer display strings, deprecated R4 device-name codes, owner/support/online-information roles, and lossy capability or physical-characteristic content.

Treat top-level `type`, property value restructuring, and output-language conversion as normal migration chores once the R6 catalog model is accepted; prioritize examples and converter tests over preserving duplicate base fields.
Track shared Resource/DomainResource behavior changes in the cross-cutting behavior review rather than as DeviceDefinition-specific blockers.

caveats: No official DeviceDefinition R4-to-R6 diff rationale, migration note, StructureMap, or ConceptMap was present in the local inputs.
Terminology judgments are based on local package artifacts, not live terminology-server expansions.
No representative production R4 DeviceDefinition corpus was available, so prevalence of optional paths is inferred rather than measured.
The R6 input is a ballot4 package and may change before final publication.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context for this DeviceDefinition review.
